items.hook: What we’re reading: writers and readers on the books they enjoyed in July
items.body:
Max Porter, Daisy Johnson, Avni Doshi and Guardian readers discuss the titles they have read over the last month. Join the conversation in the comments

items.hook: How Dolly Parton told her life story through six iconic songs
items.body: A legendary singer-songwriter, her music covered themes around love, loss, female empowerment and spirituality.

items.hook: ‘Environmental violence’: inside the fight to save indigenous land from becoming a nuclear dumping ground
items.body:
New documentary To Use a Mountain spotlights the pain and triumph of resisting government efforts to turn parts of rural US into disposal sites

Nuclear energy

items.body:
A terminally ill woman makes a final trip to Egypt in an exquisitely wrought portrait of end-of-life reckoning

items.hook: Metropolis light transport (MLT) is a global illumination application of a Monte Carlo method called the Metropolis–Hastings algorithm to the rendering equation for generating images from detailed physical descriptions of three-dimensional scenes.
items.body: One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: South Korea selects Lee Chang-dong’s ‘Possible Love’ for Oscars
items.body: The drama is set to premiere at Venice and Toronto film festivals.

items.hook: Southeast Michigan, also called southeastern Michigan, is a region in the Lower Peninsula of Michigan that is home to a majority of the state's businesses and industries as well as slightly over half of the state's population, most of whom are concentrated in Metro Detroit.
items.body: One of those things you can't un-know.

items.opener: Here's one for the group chat —
items.hook: Cyclopyrimorate is a selective pyridazine herbicide, used to control broadleaf weeds and grassy weeds, on cereals and rice.
items.body: It was launched in 2019 in Japan, and is also used in China. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: Cirsium fontinale, the fountain thistle, is a flowering perennial herb in the family Asteraceae.
items.body: It is endemic to California. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: Fernando López Tuero (1857–1907) was a Spanish agronomist who worked for several years in Puerto Rico during the final decade of Spanish colonial rule.
items.body: He is best known for identifying the white grub, larvae of scarab beetles of the genus Phyllophaga, as the cause of the 1890s sugarcane epidemic on the island. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: World War II: Chad becomes the first French colony to join the Allies under the administration of Félix Éboué, France's first black colonial governor.
items.body: World War II, or the Second World War, was a global conflict between two coalitions: the Allies and the Axis powers. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: Two U.S. journalists are shot and killed by a disgruntled former coworker while conducting a live report in Moneta, Virginia.
items.body: On the morning of August 26, 2015, news reporter Alison Parker and photojournalist Adam Ward, both employees of CBS affiliate WDBJ in Roanoke, Virginia, United States, were fatally shot while conducting a live television interview near Smith Mountain Lake in Moneta. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: World War I: The German colony of Togoland surrenders to French and British forces after a 20-day campaign. Togoland is the first German colony to fall to Allied hands in World War I.
items.body: World War I, or the First World War, also known as the Great War, was a global conflict between two coalitions: the Allies and the Central Powers. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: The Jay Report into the Rotherham child sexual exploitation scandal is published.
items.body: From the late 1980s until 2013, group-based child sexual exploitation affected an estimated 1,400 girls, generally from care home backgrounds, in the town of Rotherham, South Yorkshire, England. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: Seam me up, Scotty! After 60 years, Star Trek has had a muppet takeover. About time too
items.body:
Star Wars has embraced the magic of puppetry since the 70s, but Trekkers have been starved of any muppet action … until now. The creators of Strange New Worlds talk about boldly sewing where no one has sewn before

It’s life, Jim –

items.hook: Hanging By a Wire review – cable car rescue documentary dangles viewers on the edge of disaster
items.body:
The extraordinary fate of eight people trapped above a chasm in Pakistan makes for a tense, skilfully assembled survival story with unexpected flashes of comedy

Survival documentaries are a weird little genre of nonfiction film-mak

items.hook: The Games of the XX Olympiad open in Munich, West Germany.
items.body: The 1972 Summer Olympics, officially known as the Games of the XX Olympiad and officially branded as Munich 1972, were an international multi-sport event held in Munich, West Germany, from 26 August to 11 September 1972. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: The first recorded ascent of Triglav, the highest mountain in Slovenia.
items.body: Triglav, with an elevation of 2,863.65 metres, is the highest mountain in Slovenia and the highest peak of the Julian Alps. One of those things you can't un-know.
